# Firmware symbols named from log strings (E-M10 Mark I, body fw 1.4)

Names that `tools/ghidra/NameFuncs.java` gave functions in the Ghidra project because they reference a
debug or log string. They are **heuristics**: each name is built from the first identifier-like token of
the first suitable string a function references, so it says what the function *mentions*, which is often
but not always what it *does*. The string is quoted in every row so the basis can be judged. Hand-analysed
symbols are in [`symbol-map.md`](symbol-map.md) and take precedence; pattern families are in
[`symbol-families.md`](symbol-families.md).

Entries whose string mentions firmware update or flash storage are left out of this file.

## Pass 2: C++ method names from log strings (Ghidra name pass 2)
Functions that reference a log string of the form `Class::method …`. `tools/ghidra/NameFuncs.java` (second
pass) named each after the first such string it references, as `<Class>__<method>_<address>`. The source
string is quoted in each row. This is a heuristic: a function can reference another method's string (for
example when it logs on behalf of a callee), so treat the class and method as likely, not proven. 1060 listed;
53 whose string mentions firmware update or flash storage are left out here.

## Pass 3: remaining functions with an identifier, source-file or module-tag string
Listed 2026-11-13 from the unlabelled functions that reference text (`research/decomp/func_strings_rt.tsv`).
Three kinds, in decreasing order of how much the name says:
- an identifier-like string (39): the function is named after it, with the address appended when the name
  was taken;
- a source-file name such as `cam.c` (93): named `<file>_fn_<address>`; this only places the function in a
  source file;
- a bracketed module tag such as `[DISP]` (62): named `<tag>_fn_<address>`, with the logged text quoted.
None of these were read. Functions whose strings concern flash memory, start-up or firmware update were
left out of this pass.
